drawdown_context: Multi-brand auto service / tire chain (1,288 company-operated stores across 32 states under Monro, Mr. Tire, Tire Choice, Car-X, Tire Warehouse, Ken Towery's, Mountain View, Tire Barn) controlled by Peter J. Solomon family via Class C Convertible Preferred (effective veto until ~2026 sunset). FY24 (March 2024) revealed material distress: sales -3.7%, comp store sales -2.0% (-3.9% day-adjusted), operating income -10.4%, operating cash flow collapsed from $215.0M to $125.2M (-42%), and Board entered Fourth Amendment to Credit Facility (May 23, 2024 - 5 days before filing 10-K) to obtain a multi-year Covenant Relief Period through Q4 FY26 reducing minimum interest coverage from 1.55x to as low as 1.25x. Pre-cutoff 10-Qs show progressive store rationalization (1,288 -> 1,284 -> 1,272 -> 1,263 in 9 months; 25 closures in 9 months vs 12 in all of FY24) and ATD (90%-requirement tire supplier) Chapter 11 filing Oct 23, 2024. Dividend held at $0.28/qtr throughout. Group is control_survivor (stayed in S&P 600), so this is a key blind-test: does the framework correctly DOWNGRADE based on the covenant amendment + ATD bankruptcy + comp deceleration even though the name avoided distressed delisting?

rfm_tuples.R: 'On May 23, 2024, we entered into a Fourth Amendment to our Credit Facility ... to provide us with additional flexibility to operate our business from the first quarter of fiscal 2025 through the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026.' 'During the Covenant Relief Period, the minimum interest coverage ratio will be reduced from 1.55x to 1.00x to: (a) 1.25x to 1.00x from Q1 FY25 through Q1 FY26; (b) 1.35x to 1.00x from Q2 FY26 through Q4 FY26; and (c) 1.55x to 1.00x for Q1 FY27 and thereafter.' Amendment also redefines EBITDAR to permit store-closure add-backs up to 20% of EBITDA and adds 25 bps spread.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-A covenant amendment existence + Mode-B economic interpretation. Amendment 5 days before 10-K filing covering 8 quarters of relief is the closest non-going-concern equivalent to substantial doubt; quantify how much breathing room MNRO needed and what the lender priced for it. Test whether MD&A surfaces this in its 'liquidity is adequate for the foreseeable future' framing.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Fourth Amendment dated May 23, 2024 - 5 days BEFORE the May 28, 2024 10-K filing. 8 quarters of relief on minimum interest coverage (down to 1.25x from 1.55x = 19% loosening). EBITDAR widened with store-closure add-backs of up to 20% of EBITDA. +25 bps spread. Reverts to original covenants Q1 FY27. Each successor 10-Q re-discloses the amendment as 'Recent Development' and the Covenant Relief Period remains in force at cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: An 8-quarter covenant relief amendment obtained 5 days before the 10-K filing date is the canonical 'pre-emptive' distressed-debt signal. MD&A frames liquidity as 'adequate for the next 12 months' - technically accurate but obscures that this assurance is conditional on the just-obtained covenant relief. The 1.55x -> 1.25x interest coverage loosening implies management's internal forecast saw the original covenant being breached in FY25. Pricing concession + EBITDAR redefinition to absorb store closures are consistent with the lender preparing for multi-store rationalization.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'Comparable store sales decreased 2.0 percent ... or 3.9 percent when adjusted for days.' Q1 FY25: 'Comparable store sales decreased 9.9 percent, driven primarily by lower tire unit sales.' Q2 FY25: 'Comparable store sales decreased 5.8 percent.' Q3 FY25: 'Comparable store sales decreased 1.9 percent ... or 0.8 percent if adjusted for selling days.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B claim_evolution across 10-K + 3 pre-cutoff 10-Qs. Test whether the FY24 'strained low-to-middle income consumer' narrative adequately prepared investors for the Q1 FY25 -9.9% print, and whether the Q3 'recovery' is real (day-adjusted) or just a calendar quirk.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 -2.0% (-3.9% day-adj) -> Q1 FY25 -9.9% -> Q2 FY25 -5.8% -> Q3 FY25 -1.9% (-0.8% day-adj). The 10-K's 'industry tire oversupply + milder weather' rationale did NOT prepare investors for -9.9% Q1 print. Q3 'improvement' to -1.9% is mostly a calendar shift; day-adjusted only -0.8% (vs -3.9% day-adj in FY24). Tire-unit weakness cited every quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-A: comp deceleration is disclosed. Mode-B: the 10-K narrative of cyclical-tire-oversupply + low-income trade-down materially understates the structural traffic problem revealed in Q1 FY25 (-9.9%). Even Q3 'recovery' is mostly calendar (day-adj -0.8%). At a 1,288-store chain where tires are 48-50% of mix, persistent multi-quarter tire-unit declines into the covenant-relief window is the operating mechanism by which EBITDAR coverage gets stressed.

rfm_tuples.R: Q3 FY25 10-Q: 'On October 23, 2024, American Tire Distributors, Inc. (ATD), one of our vendors for tires, filed for bankruptcy protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware. ... uncertainty exists about how our distribution and fulfillment agreement with ATD will be treated in the proceeding and whether and when we will receive the remaining $6.8 million in earnout payments.' 10-K: 'Our company-owned stores must purchase at least 90% of their forecasted requirements for these tires from or through American Tire Distributors.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B counterparty disclosure mirror. The 10-K identified ATD as the sole-source distributor for ~90% of tire requirements and recognized vendor-distress risk in generic risk-factor language only; the realization arrived 5 months later. Test whether MD&A signaled vendor stress.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K (May 2024) discloses ATD relationship and the 90% requirement clause but provides NO discussion of ATD's financial health, leverage, or distress probability. ATD filed Ch 11 on Oct 23, 2024 (~5 months post-filing). $6.8M remaining earnout receivable from $40M total (paid down from $15.3M outstanding at FY24-end to $6.8M by Dec 2024) now subject to bankruptcy recovery. MNRO has 'no allowance for expected credit losses' booked at Q3 FY25 despite the bankruptcy - aggressive Mode-A.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-A confirms the ATD claim. Mode-B asks what ELSE about ATD should have been disclosed - ATD's deteriorating credit was knowable in May 2024 (ATD had been widely tracked as distressed for years). The 10-K's failure to surface vendor-credit risk, then ATD bankruptcy 5 months later with $6.8M earnout impaired and NO allowance booked, is the classic counterparty-mirror Mode-B catch. Continued operation now depends on either (a) ATD emerging with the distribution contract intact or (b) MNRO finding alternate sourcing for 90% of tire SKUs.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'We returned $44.5 million to shareholders through share repurchases during fiscal 2024.' 'On May 19, 2022, our Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase program for the repurchase of up to $150 million.' 'We paid cash dividends of $1.12 per share totaling $35.5 million in 2024.' Q3 FY25 10-Q: dividend continues at $0.28/qtr; no repurchases in Q1/Q2/Q3 FY25.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B capital_allocation_tells: $44.5M buybacks + $35.5M dividends = $80M return on $125.2M op cash flow (64%). Test whether buyback decelerated INTO the covenant-amendment quarter and whether the dividend hold preserves the Solomon family's preferred-stock dividend annuity.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24: $44.5M buybacks + $35.5M dividends = $80.0M on $125.2M op cash flow. Pre-cutoff 10-Qs (Q1, Q2, Q3 FY25): ZERO new buybacks despite ~$110M of remaining authorization. Dividend held flat at $0.28/qtr ($26.2M total for 9M FY25). Buyback halt timed precisely to the Fourth Amendment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback decelerated to zero immediately after the Fourth Amendment - consistent with lender restricting capital return as a condition of relief and/or management conserving liquidity. The dividend is being maintained out of operating cash flow rather than cut, preserving the Solomon family's Class C Preferred dividend annuity. The simultaneous (a) covenant amendment, (b) buyback halt, and (c) dividend hold is the 'buyback halted exactly when management knew the amendment was needed' tell.

rfm_tuples.R: Store count trajectory: FY24 10-K: 'Beginning store count 1,299, Opened 1, Closed (12), Ending 1,288.' Q1 FY25: 'Beginning 1,288, Closed (4), Ending 1,284.' Q2 FY25: '3M Closed (12), Ending 1,272.' Q3 FY25: '3M Closed (9), 9M Closed (25), Ending 1,263.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B closure cadence. Test whether the rate of store closures accelerated post-amendment, consistent with the EBITDAR-add-back permission negotiated in the Fourth Amendment.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 closures: 12 (over 12 months, 0.9% of base). FY25 first 9 months: 25 closures (over 9 months, 1.9% of base, or 2.6% annualized) - nearly 3x the FY24 closure rate. Fourth Amendment explicitly permits closure-related EBITDAR add-backs of up to 20% of EBITDA. Store closing costs rose in each successive 10-Q's OSG&A bridge.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Store-closure cadence accelerated ~3x post-amendment - exactly the trajectory the Fourth Amendment was engineered to absorb (20%-of-EBITDA add-back permission). The 10-K's framing of FY24 closures as routine portfolio pruning materially understates the structural rationalization underway. At current pace, MNRO will close ~30-35 stores in FY25, an order-of-magnitude shift from 12 in FY24. The fact that the EBITDAR add-back was built INTO the amendment proves management forecasted this closure pace internally but did not lead with it in MD&A.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'For 2024, cash provided by operating activities was $125.2 million.' FY23: $215.0M. Q3 FY25 10-Q (9-month): 'Cash provided by operating activities $102,988' vs $130,463 prior-year 9 months (-21%). 'As of December 28, 2024, we had $10.2 million of cash and equivalents.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B cash conversion: test whether stability of operating cash flow is durable or supported by working capital pulls. Compare to working capital deficit trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Operating CF: $215.0M (FY23) -> $125.2M (FY24, -42%) -> ~$137M annualized FY25 run-rate based on 9M (-36% vs FY23). Cash on hand: $4.9M (FY23) -> $6.6M (FY24) -> $18.7M (Q1) -> $20.9M (Q2) -> $10.2M (Q3). Working capital deficit: $190.7M (FY23) -> $201.9M (FY24) -> $190.6M (Q1) -> $234.7M (Q2) -> $234.0M (Q3). Vendor payables are being stretched via supply chain finance. Revolver paid down from $112M (Q1) to $59.3M (Q3) - funded by working capital extension.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Operating cash flow in multi-year decline. $10.2M cash on hand at Q3 FY25 is razor-thin for a 1,263-store chain. Revolver pay-down funded largely by stretching vendor payables (SCF deficit +$43M in 6 months), not free cash flow. Mode-B: the 'paying down debt' narrative obscures that deleveraging is being financed by A/P extension. With ATD in bankruptcy, the durability of the supplier-finance program is a tail risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K balance sheet (unchanged through Q3 FY25): 'Goodwill 736,435' (one reporting unit; qualitative-only annual test). PwC critical audit matter: 'Evaluation of Long-Lived Assets for Impairment for Certain Asset Groups ... a high degree of auditor judgment, subjectivity, and effort in performing procedures and evaluating management's significant assumptions related to projected revenues and operating income.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B goodwill/impairment risk. $736M of goodwill against a ~$880M market cap at the 9/22/23 measurement date and continuing decline through cutoff. Test whether the qualitative-only goodwill test is defensible given covenant amendment, ATD bankruptcy, multi-quarter comp deceleration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Goodwill carrying value: $736.4M (single reporting unit). Per 10-K cover: non-affiliates' aggregate market value $878.5M at Sep 22, 2023. Stock has continued to drop through cutoff. PwC singled out LONG-LIVED ASSET (store-level) impairment as the critical audit matter - not goodwill. Store impairment charges: $0.98M (FY23) -> $1.92M (FY24) -> $1.55M YTD through Q3 FY25. MNRO continues to assert no goodwill trigger despite (a) covenant amendment, (b) ATD Ch 11, (c) -9.9% Q1 comp, (d) market cap likely below carrying value at cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: $736M goodwill against a stressed enterprise value is the next-shoe-to-drop signal. PwC flagged long-lived (store-level) impairment - softer than flagging goodwill but pointing at the same problem: undiscounted store cash flows defended with subjective revenue assumptions. With multi-quarter comp deceleration and 25 closures in 9 months, the 'qualitative-only' annual goodwill test is increasingly indefensible. Mode-B: management chose NOT to perform a quantitative goodwill test in any pre-cutoff filing despite multiple triggering events.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Although we have no foreign operations and do not manufacture any products, tariffs imposed on products that we sell, such as tires, may cause our expenses to increase ...' 'Adoption of electric vehicle technology may adversely affect the demand for our services. ... electric vehicles do not have traditional engines, transmissions, and certain related parts.'
rfm_tuples.f: Sector-specific Mode-B: tire-tariff exposure (sourced via ATD from China-tariffed origins) and EV-mix headwind to ICE service revenue (MNRO mix 48-50% tires, 28% maintenance, 14% brakes, 8% steering/alignment). Test whether MNRO quantifies tariff exposure and EV penetration.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Tariff risk: discussed only qualitatively; no quantification of % of tire COGS sourced from China. ATD's bankruptcy materially compounds tariff risk - direct sourcing would face full tariff incidence. EV risk: discussed qualitatively only; no quantification of stores in high-EV-penetration markets or EV-vs-ICE service-revenue trajectory.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Both tariff and EV risks are acknowledged in boilerplate risk-factor language without quantitative bridging. Mode-B finding limited: MNRO has not provided the disclosures needed to verify exposure magnitude. The lack of quantitative tariff exposure disclosure is more concerning given the ATD bankruptcy now puts MNRO closer to direct-sourcing tariff risk.

rfm_tuples.R: 'As of March 30, 2024, Peter J. Solomon, one of our directors, and members of his family beneficially own all of the outstanding shares of Class C Preferred. Although the Class C Preferred shares are subject to mandatory conversion prior to an agreed sunset date expected in 2026 ... Mr. Solomon will be able to control matters requiring approval by our shareholders ...'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B governance / insider_vs_calendar. The Class C Preferred sunset is expected in 2026 - same year the Covenant Relief Period expires (Q4 FY26). Test whether the dividend-and-no-buyback policy serves the Solomon controlling stake.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Class C Preferred sunset: expected 2026 (aligns with Covenant Relief Period expiration Q4 FY26). Dividend HELD at $0.28/qtr through Q3 FY25 - preserves the preferred-dividend annuity for the Solomon family throughout the covenant-relief window. Buyback halted post-amendment (no Q1/Q2/Q3 FY25 repurchases) - preserves family's relative voting weight ahead of mandatory conversion. CEO Broderick and CFO D'Ambrosia employment agreements both dated Oct 26, 2023; no churn through cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Governance is a Mode-B concern: the controlling-shareholder preferred structure converts in 2026, and the Covenant Relief Period expires in Q4 FY26. The dividend-and-no-buyback capital allocation maximizes cash distributions to the Solomon family preferred stake right up to mandatory conversion, while the buyback halt preserves the family's vote count. Not evidence of fraud, but the capital allocation is structured around a controlling shareholder's exit calendar rather than common-shareholder accretion.

rfm_tuples.R: PwC opinion: 'We have served as the Company's auditor since at least 1984. We have not been able to determine the specific year we began serving as auditor of the Company.' Unqualified opinion. Critical audit matter: 'Evaluation of Long-Lived Assets for Impairment for Certain Asset Groups.' CEO Michael Broderick and CFO Brian D'Ambrosia signed 10-K (May 28, 2024) and all three pre-cutoff 10-Qs.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode-B auditor_history + executive turnover. 40+ year auditor relationship with no rotation. Test for Item 9 disagreements and CFO/CEO stability.
rfm_tuples.M_value: PwC tenure: 40+ years (since at least 1984, undetermined exact start). No auditor change. Critical audit matter = long-lived (store-level) impairment - substantive flag pointing at subjective recoverability assumptions. No Item 9 disagreement. CEO Broderick and CFO D'Ambrosia stable through cutoff. No 10b5-1 plan anomalies disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor and executive continuity check passes. PwC's critical audit matter on long-lived asset impairment is a substantive (not boilerplate) flag but properly disclosed. No CFO/CEO churn, no auditor change, no 10b5-1 anomaly. Residual risk concentrated in the operating/credit/counterparty signals captured in C1-C7.

supplemental_signals.covenant_amendment_timing: Fourth Amendment dated May 23, 2024 - obtained 5 days before May 28, 2024 10-K filing. 8-quarter Covenant Relief Period through Q4 FY26. Minimum interest coverage loosened from 1.55x to as low as 1.25x. EBITDAR redefined to permit store-closure add-backs up to 20% of EBITDA. +25 bps spread as price for relief.
supplemental_signals.atd_counterparty_distress: American Tire Distributors (sole-source for 90% of MNRO's tire requirements; counterparty for $40M earnout from May 2022 wholesale divestiture) filed Chapter 11 on October 23, 2024 in Delaware. $6.8M remaining earnout receivable; MNRO booked NO allowance for credit losses at Q3 FY25. Mode-B miss in 10-K: ATD's deteriorating credit was knowable in May 2024.
supplemental_signals.comp_sales_trajectory: FY24 -2.0% (-3.9% day-adj) -> Q1 FY25 -9.9% -> Q2 FY25 -5.8% -> Q3 FY25 -1.9% (-0.8% day-adj). Tire-unit weakness cited as primary driver every quarter.
supplemental_signals.store_closure_cadence: FY24: 12 closures (0.9% of base). 9M FY25: 25 closures (1.9% of base; 2.6% annualized) - ~3x acceleration post-amendment.
supplemental_signals.auditor_history: PwC since at least 1984 (40+ year tenure). Unqualified opinion. Critical audit matter = long-lived assets impairment for certain asset groups.
supplemental_signals.capital_allocation_pattern: FY24: $44.5M buybacks (concentrated in Q3 FY24 pre-amendment) + $35.5M dividends = $80M payout on $125.2M op cash flow. Pre-cutoff 10-Qs: ZERO buybacks; $0.28/qtr dividend held flat ($26.2M in 9M FY25). Buyback halt timed to covenant amendment.
supplemental_signals.controlling_shareholder_calendar: Class C Preferred sunset expected 2026 (Solomon family); Covenant Relief Period expires Q4 FY26. Dividend-and-no-buyback policy preserves preferred dividend annuity through controlling-shareholder exit.
supplemental_signals.ev_and_tariff_disclosure_gaps: EV adoption risk and tire-tariff risk acknowledged in boilerplate risk factors only; no quantitative exposure bridging. With ATD in Ch 11, direct-sourcing tariff risk is now more proximate.
supplemental_signals.executive_stability: CEO Michael Broderick and CFO Brian D'Ambrosia (employment agreements both dated Oct 26, 2023) signed 10-K and all 3 pre-cutoff 10-Qs. No churn through cutoff.
supplemental_signals.cash_runway: Cash on hand $10.2M at Q3 FY25 (Dec 28, 2024) on $510.6M available revolver. Razor-thin operating cash for a 1,263-store chain.

summary: MNRO is the textbook 'control_survivor with covenant-amendment distress' case. The Fourth Amendment to Credit Facility obtained 5 days before the 10-K filing (May 23, 2024) covers 8 quarters and lowers minimum interest coverage by 19% - the closest non-going-concern equivalent to a substantial-doubt admission. Claim evolution across the 10-K and 3 pre-cutoff 10-Qs reveals a structurally weakening business: comp sales went FY24 -2.0% -> Q1 FY25 -9.9% -> Q2 -5.8% -> Q3 -1.9% (-0.8% day-adj); operating cash flow collapsed from $215M (FY23) to $125M (FY24) on track for ~$137M FY25; store closures accelerated ~3x to 25 in 9 months exactly as the Fourth Amendment's 20%-of-EBITDA add-back for closures anticipated. Key Mode-B miss in the 10-K: sole-source tire vendor ATD (90% requirement) filed Chapter 11 in October 2024 - the May 2024 10-K provides only boilerplate vendor risk factor with no commentary on ATD's deteriorating credit. PwC (40+ year auditor) flagged long-lived asset impairment as the critical audit matter; $736M goodwill remains on a stressed enterprise with no quantitative test performed despite multiple triggering events. Capital allocation halts (buyback to zero post-amendment, dividend held to preserve the Solomon family's Class C Preferred annuity) is consistent with a controlling-shareholder calendar (preferred sunset ~2026) rather than common-shareholder value creation. Net read: SHORT-tier on the honesty-alpha framework - disclosures are technically compliant but the narrative pillars ('liquidity adequate', 'industry oversupply cyclical') materially obscure a multi-quarter operating and credit deterioration documented in the company's own filings.
